name: Active Directory Lateral Movement & Dominance
description: Methodology for Active Directory post-foothold attacks. Covers DCSync NTDS password dumping, Pass-the-Hash, AD CS certificate template abuse, and Golden Tickets.

steps.title: DCSync Domain NTDS Password Hash Extraction
steps.purpose: Impersonate a Domain Controller using DS-Replication permissions to dump all user NTLM hashes directly from Active Directory.
common_mistakes: User must have `Replicating Directory Changes` rights (Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins, or delegated sync accounts).
steps.if_success: Domain-wide compromise! Captured Administrator and krbtgt NTLM hashes.
steps.if_failure: Insufficient replication privileges. Check BloodHound for ACL abuse paths to Domain Admin.

steps.title: Pass-the-Hash Remote Command Execution
steps.purpose: Execute commands on any domain host using an extracted NTLM password hash without cracking the cleartext password.
common_mistakes: Passing the LM hash; place a colon before the 32-character NTLM hash: `-hashes :31d6cfe...`.
steps.if_success: Interactive Administrator shell spawned over WMI!
steps.if_failure: WMI blocked. Try `impacket-psexec` or `evil-winrm -H {{HASH}}`.

name: Advanced Active Directory (NoPac, PetitPotam, Trusts)
description: Methodology for critical domain privilege escalation: NoPac sAMAccountName Spoofing (CVE-2021-42278/42287), PetitPotam AD CS Certificate Relay, Responder LLMNR Poisoning, and Cross-Forest Domain Trusts.

steps.title: LLMNR / NBT-NS Poisoning (Responder)
steps.purpose: Poison broadcast LLMNR/NBT-NS queries on the local subnet to capture NetNTLMv2 hashes or relay authentication.
expected_output: [+] [LLMNR]  Poisoned answer sent to 10.10.10.50 for name WIN-SRV
common_mistakes: Turn off `SMB = Off` and `HTTP = Off` in `/etc/responder/Responder.conf` if using ntlmrelayx instead.
steps.if_success: NetNTLMv2 hash captured! Crack with Hashcat mode 5600.
steps.if_failure: No broadcast traffic. Trigger artificial SMB traffic with `xp_dirtree` or browser UNC paths.

steps.title: NoPac Domain Controller Takeover (CVE-2021-42278 / 42287)
steps.purpose: Exploit sAMAccountName spoofing to obtain a Kerberos Service Ticket for the Domain Controller as DA without admin credentials.
common_mistakes: Standard user must have permission to create a machine account (`MachineAccountQuota` > 0).
steps.if_success: Full Domain Controller takeover! Dumped all domain credentials.
steps.if_failure: Domain Controller is patched (post-Nov 2021 update). Test AD CS or DCSync.

steps.title: PetitPotam MS-EFSRPC & AD CS NTLM Relay
steps.purpose: Coerce Domain Controller authentication over MS-EFSRPC and relay it to AD CS Web Enrollment to obtain a machine certificate for the DC.
expected_output: [*] Requesting certificate for DC$ from CA...
common_mistakes: Request TGT with `gettgtpkinit.py` using the base64 certificate to get DC Kerberos ticket.
steps.if_success: Domain Controller certificate acquired! Generate Golden Ticket with krbtgt.
steps.if_failure: EPA (Extended Protection for Authentication) enabled on AD CS or MS-EFSRPC filtered.

name: Active Directory Certificate Services (AD CS & Certipy)
description: Comprehensive methodology from Orange Cyberdefense mindmap for auditing and exploiting AD CS certificate templates (ESC1-ESC8), Shadow Credentials, and Pass-the-Certificate.

steps.title: AD CS Vulnerable Certificate Template Discovery (Certipy)
steps.purpose: Query Active Directory Certificate Services to detect misconfigured and exploitable certificate templates (ESC1, ESC2, ESC3, ESC4, ESC8).
expected_output: ESC1: Client Authentication, Enrollee Supplies Subject, Any Purpose
common_mistakes: Not supplying `-dc-ip` if DNS is unable to resolve Domain Controller FQDN.
steps.if_success: Vulnerable ESC template found! Request administrative certificate.
steps.if_failure: No ESC1-ESC4 templates found. Check Web Enrollment NTLM relay (ESC8).

steps.title: ESC1 Template Request with Administrator UPN SAN
steps.purpose: Request an enrollment certificate supplying the Domain Administrator UPN as an alternate Subject Alternative Name (SAN).
expected_output: [*] Saved certificate and private key to `administrator.pfx`
common_mistakes: Ensure template name and CA name match exact casing from `certipy find` output.
steps.if_success: `administrator.pfx` certificate generated! Authenticate via PKINIT / Pass-the-Certificate.
steps.if_failure: Certificate enrollment rejected (Approval required). Check ESC8 relay.

steps.title: Pass-the-Certificate & NTLM Hash Extraction
steps.purpose: Authenticate against the Domain Controller using the `.pfx` certificate to retrieve the Administrator TGT and plaintext NTLM hash.
common_mistakes: Sync your clock with the DC if Kerberos rejects timestamp.
steps.if_success: Domain Administrator NTLM hash dumped! Full domain compromise.
steps.if_failure: PKINIT not supported on DC. Use certificate with Schannel LDAP binding.

steps.title: Shadow Credentials Attack (msDS-KeyCredentialLink)
steps.purpose: If you have GenericWrite/WriteProperty on a user or computer account, write shadow credentials to take over the account without changing its password.
common_mistakes: Requires functional KDC PKINIT support on the Domain Controller.
steps.if_success: Shadow credentials injected and target account hash retrieved! Proceed to DCSync.
steps.if_failure: Write permission missing on target object. Check BloodHound for ACL write paths.

steps.purpose: Collect all AD users, groups, computers, sessions, trusts, and ACLs remotely from Linux using valid domain credentials.
expected_output: [+] Dumping domain users, groups, computers, trusts...

steps.if_success: BloodHound ZIP archive generated. Import into Neo4j/BloodHound GUI for graph analysis.
steps.if_failure: LDAP authentication failed or LDAPS required. Check credentials or try `-s` for SSL LDAP.

expected_output: [*] SharpHound Enumeration Completed. Zip file written to C:\Windows\Temp\bh_data.zip

common_mistakes: BloodHound node names are uppercase (e.g. `USER@DOMAIN.LOCAL`).
steps.if_success: Actionable attack path identified! Execute specific ACL abuse or session takeover.
steps.if_failure: No direct path from current user. Expand search to all Kerberoastable or AS-REP roastable accounts.

steps.title: Abuse GenericAll / GenericWrite on Target User or Group
steps.purpose: Leverage full control (GenericAll) or WriteDacl permissions on an AD object to reset password, grant rights, or add user to Domain Admins.
steps.command: netexec smb {{TARGET}} -u '{{USERNAME}}' -p '{{PASSWORD}}' -d '{{DOMAIN|corp.local}}' -M dacl -o ACTION=add-member TARGET_GROUP='Domain Admins' USER='{{USERNAME}}'
expected_output: [+] Successfully added user to group: Domain Admins
common_mistakes: Ensure you have write permission on the target group object or WriteDacl.
steps.if_success: Current user added to Domain Admins! Relog or request new TGT.
steps.if_failure: Insufficient permissions. Check BlooHound for intermediary objects (e.g. nested group memberships).

name: Kerberos Delegation & RBCD Exploitation

steps.if_failure: Write permission missing on target computer object.

steps.purpose: Abuse Constrained Delegation with Protocol Transition (S4U2Self / S4U2Proxy) to request a service ticket for any user (including Domain Admin).

name: Active Directory Domain Persistence

steps.if_failure: LSASS protected by RunAsPPL or EDR blocked in-memory patching.

steps.purpose: Add GenericAll permissions for an unprivileged user on `CN=AdminSDHolder,CN=System,DC=corp,DC=local`. The SDProp process will automatically grant DA access every 60 minutes.

steps.if_failure: Insufficient permissions to modify AdminSDHolder container.

steps.purpose: Synchronize the local DSRM administrator password with a domain account and enable network logon (behavior 2) to maintain a stealthy local admin backdoor on DCs.
steps.command: powershell -ep bypass -c "Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\\System\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Lsa' -Name 'DsrmAdminLogonBehavior' -Value 2 -Type DWord; ntdsutil \"set dsrm password\" \"sync from domain account {{USERNAME}}\" q q"

common_mistakes: Requires domain trust or schema-level privileges if done across trusts.
steps.if_success: Target standard user now possesses Domain Admin token privileges when logging in!
steps.if_failure: DC Auditing or protected account restriction.

name: Kerberos Tickets (Golden, Silver & Pass-the-Ticket)
description: Deep exploitation guide for forging Golden Tickets (krbtgt), Silver Tickets (CIFS, HTTP, MSSQL, HOST, WSMAN), Pass-the-Ticket injection, and lateral movement using forged TGS/TGT tickets.

steps.title: Forge Silver Ticket for Target Service (Impacket ticketer.py)
steps.purpose: Forge an offline Kerberos Service Ticket (TGS) using the target service account NTLM/AES hash to access specific service (CIFS, HTTP, MSSQL) without contacting DC.
common_mistakes: Domain SID must be obtained from user account `whoami /user` or `lookupsid.py`.
SPN format must match target service hostname exactly (e.g. `cifs/target.corp.local` or `MSSQLSvc/db.corp.local:1433`).
steps.if_success: Silver Ticket `Administrator.ccache` generated! Set `KRB5CCNAME` and use ticket.
steps.if_failure: Invalid service hash or mismatched domain SID. Validate with `lookupsid.py`.

steps.title: Forge Silver Ticket & Inject via Mimikatz (Windows)
steps.purpose: Generate a Silver Ticket in memory on a Windows compromised host and immediately inject it into the current logon session (Pass-the-Ticket).
expected_output: Gold Ticket successfully submitted for current session
common_mistakes: RC4 requires NTLM hash of the computer account (e.g. `DC01$`) or service account, NOT the administrator account.
steps.if_success: Ticket injected! Access target service immediately with `dir \\\\dc.corp.local\\c$`.
steps.if_failure: Verify SPN service name matches target (cifs, http, mssql, host, wsman).

steps.title: Forge Golden Ticket with krbtgt Hash (Full Domain Compromise)
steps.purpose: Forge an offline Kerberos Ticket Granting Ticket (TGT) using the domain `krbtgt` NTLM or AES-256 key to achieve total domain persistence and admin access to any service.
common_mistakes: krbtgt hash must be acquired via DCSync (`secretsdump.py`).
steps.if_success: Golden Ticket generated! Authenticate against any domain service for up to 10 years.
steps.if_failure: Ensure correct domain SID format and krbtgt NTLM hash.

steps.title: Pass-the-Ticket (PTT) Execution on Linux
steps.purpose: Export the forged or extracted `.ccache` ticket into the Linux environment variable `KRB5CCNAME` and execute remote administrative commands.
common_mistakes: Target must be referenced by FQDN (e.g. `dc.corp.local`), NOT by raw IP, when using Kerberos authentication.
Ensure system time is synchronized with DC within 5 minutes (`sudo rdate -n <DC_IP>` or `ntpdate`).
steps.if_success: Authenticated via Kerberos ticket! Run `psexec.py -k -no-pass` or `smbexec.py -k -no-pass` for interactive SYSTEM shell.
steps.if_failure: Time skew error or FQDN not in `/etc/hosts`. Add `<DC_IP> <DOMAIN> <DC_HOSTNAME>.<DOMAIN>` to `/etc/hosts`.

name: DNS Zone Transfers & Fuzzing (Port 53)

steps.if_failure: No new subdomains. Check standard HTTP web directories on port 80/443.

steps.purpose: Query specialized DNS records (TXT, SRV, CNAME) which often disclose API tokens, SPF records, or Active Directory service locations.

steps.if_success: Discovered critical internal services and Active Directory domain controllers.

steps.title: FTP Anonymous Login Check (NetExec)
steps.purpose: Verify if the FTP service allows unauthenticated (anonymous:anonymous) read/write access.

expected_output: | ftp-anon: Anonymous FTP login allowed (FTP code 230)

steps.if_success: Identified exact FTP server version and configuration. Check for known CVE exploits.
steps.if_failure: No immediate vulnerabilities found. Proceed to credential bruteforcing or file download.

steps.purpose: Download all accessible directories, files, and hidden archives from the FTP server to your local machine for offline inspection.

steps.purpose: Test candidate usernames against common wordlists when default or anonymous credentials fail.

steps.if_success: Valid FTP credentials found! Log in and inspect private user home directories.
steps.if_failure: Bruteforce unsuccessful. Pivot to other open service ports.

steps.if_failure: Generic response. Proceed to directory and virtual host discovery.

steps.title: Directory & File Discovery (ffuf)
steps.purpose: Fuzz for hidden administration panels, backup files, `.git` repositories, configuration files, and API routes.
common_mistakes: Not fuzzing file extensions (`-e .php,.txt,.bak,.json`); hidden backup files are high-value targets.
steps.if_success: Discovered hidden paths! Browse to discovered endpoints and inspect source code.

steps.purpose: Detect virtual hosts on the same IP by fuzzing the `Host:` request header.

steps.if_success: Virtual host found! Add to `/etc/hosts` and scan the newly mapped application.
steps.if_failure: No virtual hosts configured. Proceed to parameter fuzzing and web vulnerability testing.

steps.title: GET / POST Parameter Discovery
steps.purpose: Discover hidden input parameters on pages that accept query strings (often vulnerable to LFI, SSRF, or SQLi).
common_mistakes: Testing only GET requests; some parameters are only processed via POST body.
steps.if_success: Input parameter found! Test for LFI (`?page=`), Command Injection (`?cmd=`), and SQLi (`?id=`).

name: IPMI Baseboard Management Controller (Port 623 UDP)

steps.title: IPMI Version & BMC Detection
steps.purpose: Query the BMC (Baseboard Management Controller) to determine IPMI version (1.5 / 2.0) and vendor (Dell iDRAC / HP iLO / Supermicro).
expected_output: | ipmi-version: IPMI-2.0, Dell iDRAC9, UserAuth: password, kgHash: default
common_mistakes: IPMI runs on UDP; use `nmap -sU`.
steps.if_success: IPMI 2.0 detected! Proceed to RAKP hash dumping.
steps.if_failure: Port closed or not IPMI. Check other services.

steps.title: Dump RAKP User Hashes (Metasploit)
steps.purpose: Exploit the IPMI 2.0 RAKP protocol flaw to request password verification hashes for any username without authentication.
steps.command: msfconsole -q -x "use auxiliary/scanner/ipmi/ipmi_dumphashes; set RHOSTS {{TARGET}}; run; exit"

name: Kerberos Attacks (Port 88)
description: Comprehensive Active Directory Kerberos attack methodology on port 88. Covers user enumeration (Kerbrute), AS-REP Roasting, Kerberoasting SPN accounts, and Pass-the-Ticket.

steps.title: Kerberos Fast User Enumeration (Kerbrute)
steps.purpose: Systematically validate domain usernames against Kerberos without generating login failure events in event logs.

steps.purpose: Request TGT tickets for accounts with DONT_REQ_PREAUTH set; tickets contain crackable encrypted hashes that require ZERO credentials.

steps.if_success: AS-REP hash extracted! Crack with Hashcat mode 18200: `hashcat -m 18200 asrep.hashes rockyou.txt`.
steps.if_failure: No accounts with Pre-Auth disabled. Proceed to Kerberoasting once valid user credentials are obtained.

steps.title: Kerberoasting (Extract Service Account TGS Hashes)
steps.purpose: Query Service Principal Names (SPNs) registered in Active Directory and extract crackable TGS ticket hashes for service accounts (e.g. MSSQL, IIS, Backup).
common_mistakes: Not testing with domain-joined guest account if no user credentials are known.
steps.if_success: TGS hash captured! Crack with Hashcat mode 13100: `hashcat -m 13100 kerberoast.hashes rockyou.txt -r best64.rule`.
steps.if_failure: No SPNs found or account credentials invalid. Check LDAP descriptions or SMB shares.

steps.title: Pass-the-Ticket (TGT / TGS Injection)
steps.purpose: Inject a captured `.ccache` or `.kirbi` Kerberos ticket into your current terminal session to execute remote commands without knowing the plaintext password.
common_mistakes: Using IP instead of Hostname/FQDN; Kerberos ticket verification strictly requires hostname matching.
steps.if_success: Administrator SYSTEM shell spawned via Kerberos ticket delegation!
steps.if_failure: Ticket expired or clock skew. Check ticket lifetime with `klist`.

steps.purpose: Query the LDAP RootDSE unauthenticated to discover domain naming contexts, domain functional level, and Forest configuration.
common_mistakes: Not specifying `-x` for simple anonymous authentication.
steps.if_success: Identified Base DN (`DC=corp,DC=local`). Proceed to anonymous object dump.
steps.if_failure: Anonymous RootDSE disabled. Try authenticated query with discovered credentials.

steps.title: Anonymous LDAP Domain Object Dump

name: CMS, Frameworks & Enterprise Apps (WordPress, Tomcat, Jenkins, Spring)
description: Targeted attack vectors for common CMS platforms (WordPress, Joomla, Drupal), Java application servers (Tomcat, WebLogic), CI/CD pipelines (Jenkins), and modern frameworks (Spring Boot, Laravel).

steps.if_failure: WordPress not detected or XML-RPC blocked.

steps.purpose: Authenticate to Tomcat Web Application Manager (`/manager/html`) with default credentials and deploy a malicious `.war` package containing a Java JSP reverse shell.

common_mistakes: In `/actuator/env`, passwords are masked with `******`. Download `/actuator/heapdump` to recover the unmasked plaintext strings.

steps.if_failure: Actuators protected or disabled (`management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=none`).

steps.title: Jenkins Groovy Script Console Remote Code Execution
steps.purpose: Execute arbitrary Groovy code as SYSTEM / root via the administrative Jenkins Script Console (`/script`).
common_mistakes: Requires CSRF crumb header if CSRF protection is enabled (`curl -s -u admin:password 'http://target:8080/crumbIssuer/api/json'`).

name: OS Command Injection & Filter Bypasses
description: Methodology for Command Injection vulnerabilities. Covers command separators (; && |), space filter bypasses (${IFS}), base64 encoding execution, and out-of-band exfiltration.

steps.title: Command Separator Discovery (; | && || `)
steps.purpose: Test command delimiters to break out of expected input and execute operating system commands.

steps.if_success: Direct command injection confirmed! Proceed to reverse shell execution.
steps.if_failure: Input sanitized. Test space bypasses with `${IFS}`.

steps.title: Space Filter Bypass via ${IFS}
steps.purpose: Bypass input filters stripping spaces using the Linux Internal Field Separator `${IFS}` variable.
common_mistakes: On Windows machines, use `%ProgramFiles:~10,1%` or redirection operators (`type<file.txt`) instead of `${IFS}`.
steps.if_success: Space filter bypassed! Use `${IFS}` to structure reverse shell payload.
steps.if_failure: Character filter active. Use Base64 pipe execution.

steps.title: Base64 Encoded Payload Execution
steps.purpose: Bypass all character filters by encoding the entire reverse shell string into Base64 and piping it to bash.
common_mistakes: Starting command before launching your netcat listener: `nc -lvnp 4444`.
steps.if_success: Interactive reverse shell received on Kali! Stabilize TTY shell.
steps.if_failure: Outbound TCP connection blocked. Try HTTP/DNS out-of-band reverse shell.

name: Web Content Discovery & Attack Surface Mapping
description: Modern methodology for discovering hidden web endpoints, virtual host subdomains (VHosts), hidden GET/POST parameters (Arjun), directory brute-forcing, and technology stack fingerprinting.

steps.title: Recursive Directory & File Fuzzing (FFUF)

steps.purpose: Fuzz the HTTP Host header to discover internal virtual hosts and hidden tenant subdomains mapped on the same IP.

steps.if_failure: No virtual hosts detected. Ensure testing both HTTP and HTTPS.

steps.title: Hidden GET/POST Parameter Discovery (Arjun)
steps.purpose: Automatically discover hidden, unlinked GET/POST parameters on web endpoints that may trigger debug features, command execution, or SQL injection.
common_mistakes: Test JSON parameter mode (-m JSON) on API routes.

steps.if_failure: No parameters found on entry script. Test individual discovered sub-paths.
